core_obligations: Reduce to Y = Spec(R) by etale locality on Y and take an arbitrary section h of O_X over X (proof lines 10158-10162).
View h as a Y-morphism X -> A^1_Y and form the scheme theoretic image Z, checking that h is quasi-compact (proof lines 10163-10173).
Show that X -> Z has dense image and is closed, hence h(X) = Z set theoretically (proof lines 10174-10177).
Apply the properness lemma to conclude that Z -> Y is universally closed, hence integral because Z -> Y is also affine (proof lines 10178-10182).
Translate integrality into the existence of a monic polynomial P in R[T] vanishing on h, i.e. P(h) = 0 (proof lines 10183-10185).
difficulty_reason: Counts the author Lemma: for a quasi-compact, quasi-separated and universally closed morphism f : X -> Y of algebraic spaces over S, the sheaf f_*O_X is integral over O_Y, so that the normalization of Y in X is the factorization through the relative spectrum of f_*O_X (source lines 10144-10156). The proof is a genuine argument: after reducing to Y = Spec(R) it takes a section h, views it as a morphism to the affine line A^1_Y, forms the scheme theoretic image Z of h, shows h is quasi-compact, hence X -> Z has dense image and — because universal closedness is preserved by the factorization — is closed, so h(X) = Z set theoretically; a properness lemma then makes Z -> Y universally closed, and Z is affine over Y, hence integral, so the ideal of Z in R[T] contains a monic polynomial P with P(h) = 0.
